stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec on a complex cross-platform CMS live-preview feature. Openspec needed first to elaborate AC across GO, UP, and MX contexts; speckit then to harden for edge cases, security, and testability. No prior hand-curation detected.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist in the codebase. Attachment points are the content delivery pipeline (useContent hook, ContentstackContext provider, contentstack service). VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. All Contentstack-dependent criteria are framed at our boundary with explicit mock assumptions.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all 16 criteria are authored from scratch based on the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' and the architectural hints in openspec's notes (useContent hook, ContentstackContext, contentstack service). Coverage: core real-time update behavior (AC 1-3), error handling and reconnection (AC 4-6), concurrent editing (AC 7), rich content (AC 8), performance (AC 9), session longevity (AC 10), security/auth (AC 11-12), accessibility (AC 13), resource cleanup (AC 14), unsupported content types (AC 15), and locale/variant switching (AC 16). All criteria are framed as observable outcomes without prescribing implementation. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: The story description is extremely minimal and no file contents were available for review. These criteria are inferred and may need adjustment once the actual codebase and CMS integration contract are examined. The 5-second latency threshold in AC 1 is a reasonable starting assumption but should be validated against the CMS's actual preview webhook/polling capabilities.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline breakdown: openspec did not produce acceptance criteria (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0) despite its stated mandate to elaborate ACs for an empty-criteria story. Speckit compensated by authoring all 16 criteria from scratch with no codebase access, self-flagging output as inferred and unvalidated. Agents did not add non-overlapping value — openspec contributed nothing actionable; speckit performed both roles. The 16 criteria cover broad dimensions (real-time updates, error handling, concurrent editing, security, accessibility, resource cleanup) but rest on ungrounded assumptions (e.g., 5-second latency threshold, Contentstack integration contract). No story splits were produced despite the cross-platform complexity (GO, UP, MX) suggesting decomposition is warranted. Human review needed to validate criteria against actual CMS contracts and determine if the story should be split.
